steps.sub: The state's rate of change is H applied to the current state

steps.label: H, the Hamiltonian, generates time evolution
steps.sub: Know H, and you know everything about the system's future

steps.label: H is Hermitian (Chapter 1's postulate 2)
steps.sub: Its eigenvalues are the system's possible energies

steps.label: This course won't solve it for real atoms
steps.sub: That's physics-major territory — the structure is what matters here

steps.label: A superposition of two solutions is itself a solution
steps.sub: This single fact guarantees superposition SURVIVES evolution

steps.label: A system in superposition stays in superposition
steps.sub: Generally a different one — evolution never collapses it on its own

steps.label: Only measurement collapses a state (Chapter 3)
steps.sub: Evolution is deterministic and linear; measurement is probabilistic

steps.label: This is the same linearity from Chapter 5's no-cloning proof
steps.sub: Not a coincidence — the same structural fact, reused

steps.label: Every gate is a snapshot of Schrödinger evolution
steps.sub: Under some deliberately engineered Hamiltonian, for a precise duration

steps.label: Gates aren't an abstraction layered on top of physics
steps.sub: They ARE physics, engineered to implement a chosen computation
